editorial:
You get a near-future thriller about a grieving detective who hunts people trading artificial humans on the black market. When an underground group sabotages the programming of his companion android, she starts acting like his late wife and questioning what is real. The movie mixes mystery, sci-fi, and emotional drama, with a dark mood and a steady sense of danger. It is not a huge blockbuster, but it keeps you curious about who is lying and what the android will do next.

The acting carries much of the tension, especially in the quieter scenes where Meredith seems confused and afraid. The pacing is mostly steady, though some twists feel familiar if you have seen other AI thrillers. The pros are the moody look, the central mystery, and the emotional hook. The cons are a few thin side characters and an ending that may leave you wanting more answers. Watch it if you like dark sci-fi mysteries.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Meredith learns she is an artificial human, her memories were planted, and the resistance used her to get close to William. The twist is that William knew more than he let on, and the last shot leaves you wondering whether she breaks free or becomes another tool in the black market for artificial humans after everything she has seen.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark sci-fi mysteries and AI thrillers.
